title: Application Window Discovery
summary: Application window discovery is the enumeration of the windows currently open on a host, normally through a scripting environment or native operating system functions that return window titles along with the process that owns each window. Every open window leaks context: which business applications run on the machine, whether a document is being edited, whether a browser session is active, and whether administrative or security consoles are present. An adversary uses that list to choose collection targets and to spot monitoring tools worth avoiding. Because the call is local, fast and unremarkable, it produces almost no network evidence. Detection therefore rests on endpoint telemetry: process creation with unusual scripting parents, script block logging, module loads for the window enumeration functions, and repeated discovery by a single process. The behaviour closely resembles legitimate software, since accessibility tools, screen readers, remote support agents and inventory products enumerate windows routinely, so the owning process, its signature and whatever happened next carry the real weight.

beginner.definition: Application window discovery means making a list of the windows that are open on a computer right now. Each window has a title, such as a document name or a program name. That list tells the attacker what the person at that computer is doing. No files are changed to obtain it.
beginner.whyItMatters: Open windows show which programs matter on a machine. They can also show whether a security console or a chat program is running. An attacker who knows this can pick what to steal and what to avoid. The request itself looks harmless, so it is easy to miss in a busy log.
howItWorks: A program asks the operating system for a list of all open windows.
For each window it reads the title text and the process that owns it.
It may also check window state, such as visible, minimised or in the background.
It turns that raw list into a short report the operator can read quickly.
It repeats the check over time to see which programs open and close.
It sends the report to the attacker or stores it for later collection.
beginner.example: Picture a shared flat where every flatmate writes their name on the bedroom door. A visitor who walks the corridor learns who is home, who is asleep, and who left a laptop charging on the desk. They do not open a single door. Application window discovery is that walk down the corridor. The names on the doors are the window titles, and they tell the visitor which room deserves a closer look later.
takeaways: Window titles leak which programs and documents are in use on a machine.
This discovery is quiet, so detection depends on endpoint telemetry, not network logs.
The same calls are normal for accessibility and support tools, so check the caller.

objectives: Explain what an open window list reveals about a user's work.
Describe how programs enumerate windows on Windows and other operating systems.
Identify the endpoint telemetry that can reveal window enumeration.
Distinguish legitimate accessibility or support tools from malicious enumeration.
Suggest ways to reduce the value of window titles to an attacker.
